definitions.explanation: To enjoy something thoroughly and to one's heart's content. Used as a suru verb.
Having a high level of skill or mastery in something, especially a language or an art. Used as a na-adjective.

examples.japanese: {京都|きょうと}の{紅葉|こうよう}を{堪能|たんのう}した。
examples.english: I fully enjoyed the autumn foliage in Kyoto.

examples.japanese: {旬|しゅん}の{魚介|ぎょかい}{料理|りょうり}を{堪能|たんのう}する。
{温泉|おんせん}に{浸|つ}かり、{地元|じもと}の{食材|しょくざい}を{使|つか}った{料理|りょうり}を{堪能|たんのう}して、{最高|さいこう}の{休日|きゅうじつ}を{過|す}ごした。
examples.english: I soaked in hot springs and savored dishes made with local ingredients — it was the best holiday.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{英語|えいご}に{堪能|たんのう}だ。
{三|さん}か{国語|こくご}に{堪能|たんのう}な{通訳者|つうやくしゃ}を{探|さが}している。
examples.english: We are looking for an interpreter fluent in three languages.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{武道|ぶどう}に{堪能|たんのう}で、{剣道|けんどう}も{柔道|じゅうどう}も{有段者|ゆうだんしゃ}だ。
examples.english: He is highly skilled in martial arts and holds dan rankings in both kendo and judo.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 1 (to enjoy fully) is used as a suru verb: ～を{堪能|たんのう}する. Very common in travel writing and food reviews. Sense 2 (proficient) is used as a na-adjective: ～に{堪能|たんのう}だ. This sense is especially common when describing language ability.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ～を{堪能|たんのう}する: to fully enjoy ~
- {料理|りょうり}を{堪能|たんのう}する: to savor a meal
- {景色|けしき}を{堪能|たんのう}する: to enjoy the scenery
- ～に{堪能|たんのう}だ: to be proficient in ~
- {語学|ごがく}に{堪能|たんのう}: proficient in languages

ETYMOLOGY:
Originally two separate words that converged. Sense 1 derives from a Buddhist term meaning "to be satisfied." Sense 2 comes from {堪|た}える{能|のう}（{力|りょく}） meaning "ability to endure/perform."
